## US Polysilicon Tariff Impact

The Trump administration has announced a 15% tariff on polysilicon and its derivative products, effective immediately. This represents a significant shift in US trade policy aimed at countering Chinese competition and expanding domestic solar production capabilities. Korean companies including Hanwha and OCI face potential headwinds from this measure, though they may benefit from opportunities in US-based manufacturing. The government has formally requested flexible application of these tariffs to minimize disruption to Korean enterprises operating within US supply chains.

## Weak US Employment Report

US employment contracted by 23,000 positions in July, an unexpected decline that has dramatically shifted market expectations for Federal Reserve policy. The unemployment rate fell to 4.10% from the previous month's 4.05%, creating mixed signals about the health of the American labor market. According to CME FedWatch data, markets now price in a 60% probability of interest rate holds at the September FOMC meeting, up sharply from 45% the previous day. This employment shock has triggered significant repricing across global financial markets as investors recalibrate their inflation and growth assumptions.

## Global Market Response

The unexpected employment weakness sent US Treasury yields plummeting, with two-year yields falling 0.07% to 4.17%. Despite traditionally negative employment news, equity markets rallied as investors grew more confident the Federal Reserve would avoid additional rate increases. The S&P 500 reached all-time highs while the Nasdaq climbed 1.3%, demonstrating the market's preference for accommodative monetary policy over tighter labor markets. Upcoming inflation data on August 12th and 13th will provide crucial signals for the September FOMC decision.

## Korea's Central Bank Holds Firm

The Bank of Korea maintained its benchmark interest rate at 2.75% in July, reflecting confidence in economic fundamentals despite external volatility. The decision was supported by continued strength in semiconductor-led exports, steady investment performance, and healthy consumer spending patterns. Real GDP growth in the first half of 2026 exceeded expectations, providing the central bank with justification for maintaining its accommodative stance. However, the rating agency Fitch cautioned that Korean stock market weakness poses greater risks to the real estate sector than financial institutions.

## Korean Stock Market Turbulence

KOSPI experienced severe volatility, plunging more than 4% on August 6th with intraday losses exceeding 5%, triggering automatic circuit breaker halts. The index had fallen from its June 19th high of 9,385.59 to 5,593.56 by July 30th, representing a 39% decline that has shaken investor confidence. KOSDAQ fell below the 800-point threshold, closing at 799.36 after six consecutive trading days of decline. Remarkably, the Korean won strengthened significantly against the dollar, declining from 1,550 won per dollar in early July to 1,416.1 won, defying typical patterns during equity market downturns.

## Real Estate Supply Response

The government has announced sweeping measures to accelerate housing supply, including expanded project finance guarantees and relaxed relocation loan regulations. Deputy Prime Minister Gu Yoon-chul indicated willingness to extend non-resident single-property tax exemptions beyond the current three-year period, suggesting flexible policy interpretation. Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon submitted a report emphasizing private redevelopment and reconstruction as primary solutions to housing supply shortages, positioning city government at odds with the administration's public-sector-led approach. The following week will see 4,808 units launched for sale nationwide, including the major Han River Prussian Riverfront development in Gimpo.

## Tax Code Revisions Impact

The government's comprehensive real estate tax reform dramatically alters the tax burden based on occupancy status and ownership structure. Identical 3-billion-won apartments now incur vastly different tax liabilities depending on whether the owner resides in the property, with primary residences receiving preferential treatment. This differentiation marks a fundamental shift from previous uniform tax treatment, creating winners and losers based on occupancy decisions rather than property values alone. The tax changes attempt to encourage residential occupation while discouraging speculation in non-primary residences.

## Industrial Innovation Initiatives

The government launched a comprehensive economic structural reform initiative emphasizing robotics, semiconductors, chemicals, steel, automotive, batteries, shipbuilding, and appliances. Samsung Electronics established a new RX Business Division dedicated to robot development, while experts identified AI semiconductors as a key recovery catalyst for August trading. Domestic researchers developed adaptive AI semiconductors that reduce prediction errors by up to 40%, positioning Korean technology competitively against global alternatives. The Industrial Ministry and Climate Ministry forged policy coordination to develop the used-battery sector, dismantling bureaucratic silos to accelerate circular economy development.

## Corporate Investment Surge

SK Hynix announced 54 trillion won in capital expenditure across new fabs in Yongin and Cheongju, advancing memory infrastructure to capture sustained AI-driven demand. Naver reported record second-quarter revenues of 3.389 trillion won driven by AI-powered advertising contributions exceeding 60% of growth, though operating profits declined 0.2% due to infrastructure investments. The expansion of power infrastructure for AI servers creates unprecedented opportunities for banking sector corporate financing, as global lenders mobilize capital for energy grid modernization across developed economies.

## Investment Implications

For Korean investors navigating this turbulent landscape, the convergence of weak US employment data, divergent monetary policy signals, and domestic structural reforms presents both risks and opportunities. The government's aggressive housing supply initiatives and corporate tax reforms should gradually stabilize real estate markets, though transition periods will create winners and losers. Semiconductor and AI-related investments benefit from long-term structural tailwinds despite short-term volatility. The strengthening won creates export headwinds but improves household purchasing power, particularly for imported goods. Monitor upcoming US inflation data closely, as August CPI and PPI figures will determine whether the Fed maintains its accommodative stance through 2026.
headline: US Tariffs Threaten Korea as Markets React to Weak Employment Data
